reasoning: Propagate an orthonormal signed four-axis frame along the guaranteed tree of eight cubes. The first three axes describe the unfolded local cube coordinates and the fourth its outward normal after folding. Crossing a shared face in signed local direction i rotates by 90 degrees: new normal is sign*axis_i and new axis_i is -sign*old_normal, leaving the other axes fixed. A tesseract has exactly the eight cubic boundary cells with normals +/- each of its four coordinate axes. The tree removes orientation consistency cycles; adjacent folded cubes share the correct square. Thus eight distinct resulting normals are exactly the condition that all eight boundary cells are covered once, while any repeated normal overlaps a cell and leaves another uncovered.
